title: Homes Around the World
strapline: Every home is different — and every home is somebody's.
intent: Looking at homes from many places helps children see that people live in wonderfully different ways, and that all are valued.
Comparing houses, flats, houseboats, homes on stilts and homes in cold and hot places builds real knowledge of the world.
Building and playing in different homes is rich construction and small-world play with a purpose.
Talking about their own home and noticing others are different grows respect and a sense of self and family.
The theme invites families in — every child's home has a story worth sharing.
implementation: Offer photos of real homes from around the world and open-ended materials so children can build their own versions.
Sit alongside and wonder: 'Why might a home be built up high on stilts? What would it be like to live on a boat?'
Invite children to talk about their own homes — who lives there, what it's like — with warmth and no comparison.
Feed in real knowledge lightly — homes near water, in hot deserts, in snowy places, and why they're built as they are.
Ask families to share a photo or a word about home, and celebrate the range across the room.
Follow the play — some children will build homes all week, others will play families living in them.
key_questions: What is your home like — who lives there with you?
Why might a house be built up on tall stilts?
How is this home different from yours — and how is it the same?
What would keep a home warm in the snow, or cool in the heat?
What does every home need, wherever it is in the world?

impact.text: Children talk about their own family and home and notice other families and homes are different.
Children build and adapt different kinds of homes with purpose.
Children learn about homes in different places and why they are built as they are.
Children show respect for ways of living that differ from their own.
Children play families and homes with shared roles and storylines.

enhancements: A homes-of-the-world photo wall with real images from many places.
Construction materials for building stilt houses, boats, tents and tall flats.
A small-world set of different home types with families to move in.
A 'my home' sharing display with family photos or drawings.
Non-fiction books about homes and daily life in different countries.

playing_exploring: Children build and play different homes, following what fascinates them.
They explore how homes are made and who lives in them.
active_learning: Children keep improving their builds until the stilt house stands or the boat floats.
They see a home-building project through from idea to family moving in.
creating_thinking: Children reason about why homes are built differently in different places.
They compare their own home with others and hold both ideas in mind.
